subject: Polar Bank SIG intake: evidence queue and clarifications
messages:
From: Linda Garcia <linda.garcia@polarbk.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: security_ops@polarbk.com
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Polar Bank SIG-Lite intake & evidence queue

Marcus,

Thanks for taking this on. Polar Bank is running a SIG-Lite intake for a planned pilot and we need a control-to-evidence mapping, plus a small set of artifacts to satisfy our security team and external auditor sampling. Attached is our SIG-Lite_Questionnaire.pdf — you'll see the controls flagged for technology vendors (sections A2-A9). Our expected timeline is a tight window: initial mapping and a partial evidence bundle by 2026-05-20, final submission by 2026-05-27.

High-priority asks:
- Confirmation of encryption-at-rest controls and a sample key rotation policy
- A sample of access logs (redacted is fine) covering the last 90 days for service accounts that interact with customer data
- SOC 2 scope statement or attestation summary (if available)

Please confirm a point of contact and whether we can use a shared Drive link for artifact pickup or if you need SFTP. If there's any policy preventing sharing of logs, flag that now so we can triage with our auditors.

Regards,
Linda
Senior Vendor Risk Analyst
Polar Bank

Attachments: SIG-Lite_Questionnaire.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Linda Garcia <linda.garcia@polarbk.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Polar Bank SIG-Lite intake & evidence queue

Hi Linda — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear timeline. We're ready to support. Quick plan from our side: 

1) I'll own the control mapping delivery (we'll populate RB_Control_Mapping_Template.xlsx and map Redwood controls to SIG questions).
2) Monica will assemble the initial evidence bundle (access logs sample, KMS/procure docs) and post to a shared Drive folder.
3) Karthik will confirm audit scope/SOC2 artifacts and provide an attestation summary.

We can use Google Drive for artifacts; I'll create a restricted folder and share the link with your team. If your auditors require SFTP, let us know and we'll open a temporary transfer.

Two immediate clarifications so we can prioritize:
- When you say "service accounts that interact with customer data," can you list which systems you're referencing (API endpoints, embedding index exports, etc.)?
- Is the 90-day log window a hard requirement for the initial submission, or is a 30-day sample acceptable for auditor triage?

We'll target the mapping XLSX and a partial evidence package by 2026-05-15 to give you something to review ahead of your 5/20 checkpoint.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachment: RB_Control_Mapping_Template.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Linda Garcia <linda.garcia@polarbk.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence: initial bundle and artifact links for Polar Bank

Linda / Marcus — attaching the initial artifact list and placing the files in the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cPolarBankEvidence

Contents posted (redacted where required):
- access-logs-sample.zip (service-account-audit-logs_2026-02-01_to_2026-04-30.csv)
- kms-procedure.pdf (key rotation SOP, redacted keys)
- idp-provisioning-snapshots.pdf (SAML group membership export)
- partial-soc2-summary.txt (high-level scope & auditor contact obscured per policy)

Notes and caveats:
- Access logs have been redacted to remove raw customer identifiers; if you need a sanitized token mapping to validate flows, we can run a scoped export with your team present.
- The KMS procedure documents our rotation cadence and roles; we cannot share HSM console screenshots but can provide timestamps of key rotations and signing events if the auditors need them.

Next steps we propose: 30-minute intake call to run through items and confirm whether 30-day vs 90-day logs are acceptable for initial review. My availability: 2026-05-14 10:00-12:00 PT or 2026-05-15 08:00-11:00 PT.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Technical Program Manager, Security & Assurance
Redwood Inference

Attachments posted: access-logs-sample.zip; kms-procedure.pdf

From: Linda Garcia <linda.garcia@polarbk.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@polarbk.com
Date: 2026-05-12T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence: initial bundle and artifact links for Polar Bank

Monica — thank you for the quick turnaround and for redacting sensitive fields. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Encryption-at-rest: our tech reviewer needs a confirmation that database and object-store volumes used for customer data are encrypted with customer-unique keys or a documented tenant separation approach. The KMS procedure looks good, but can you confirm whether customer contexts use separate keys or a multi-tenant key envelope pattern?
- Retention: we need your documented retention policy for logs and snapshots (we asked for retention policy sample in the SIG matrix). Can you post the policy excerpt to the Drive folder?
- SOC2 auditor: is there a contact point we can provide to our vendor risk team to confirm scope? An auditor name + high-level report date is sufficient (we don't need the full report yet).

We'd like confirmation on the above by EOD 2026-05-13 so our audit window doesn't slip. If that's not possible, please propose the earliest time you can provide those items.

Thanks,
Linda

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Linda Garcia <linda.garcia@polarbk.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence: initial bundle and artifact links for Polar Bank

Linda — thanks for the questions, we can cover all three items. Quick responses: 

- Encryption model: Redwood uses a tenant-aware envelope encryption pattern. Per-tenant data encryption keys (DEKs) are wrapped by a master key in KMS; we can provide a high-level diagram and a sanitized table showing rotation timestamps without exposing key material. We'll add a short note to the Drive folder (kms-encryption-model-summary.pdf).
- Retention policy: attaching a policy excerpt to the Drive folder now (redwood-retention-policy_excerpt.pdf). It documents log retention ranges and restoration windows.
- SOC 2 contact: our auditor is Brightshore LLP, report issued 2025-11-18. Point of contact: auditmanager@brightshore-llp.com (we will provide a one-line attestation summary in the mapping spreadsheet).

Action items and owners: 
- Marcus: populate the mapping XLSX with the SOC2 control references (target 2026-05-14 EOD).
- Monica: post kms-encryption-model-summary.pdf and redwood-retention-policy_excerpt.pdf (done).
- Karthik: reach out to Brightshore to confirm a short attestation line and share contact for your vendor-risk team (in progress).

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute call on 2026-05-14 at 10:00 PT to walk through the mapping and any remaining evidence gaps. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite to your team.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
